text:
Rasmus Dahlin and the Sabres have had a rough November: five straight losses before Thursday's 6-3 win in Washington, where the captain scored and set up another, then a 4-3 loss in Florida on Saturday. The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn called the Washington game "a night Rasmus Dahlin and the rest of this team badly needed".

His season line is quiet by his standards: 14 points in 20 games, 1.70 points per 60, below our talent range for him (1.78 to 2.40). The underlying play is fine, though. Buffalo controls 52.1% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, 3.8 points better than without him, and neither his own finishing nor his teammates' looks unlucky. Evolving-Hockey had him 12th among defensemen in 2025-26, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.2 primary shot assists per 60, 99th percentile at his position.

He is carrying a big load, 24.7 minutes a night. If the setups start turning into goals, the points should rise toward our range of 54 to 78 for the season. A Sabres turnaround probably runs through him.
